info.name: archival-rag ragsvc
info.description:
HTTP API the Drupal chatbot module calls. Three endpoint groups:

- **Health** — GET /health, no auth, liveness + collection size.
- **Chat** — POST /chat (full answer) and POST /chat/stream (SSE tokens). This is the endpoint the chatbot widget actually needs.
- **Ingest** — POST /ingest (sync) / /ingest/async + GET /status/{job_id}. Used by the Node-RED indexing flow, not by Drupal's chat UI.

Set the `baseUrl` collection variable to wherever ragsvc is running (`http://127.0.0.1:8000` for local dev via `make api`, or the GPU VM host — see docs/deploying-ragsvc.md). **Use `127.0.0.1`, not `localhost`, for local testing on Mac** — Docker Desktop's background process can also bind port 8000 over IPv6, and `localhost` may resolve to that dead end instead of your actual server (symptom: request just fails/hangs with no response). If the server has `EMBEDDING_API_KEY` configured, also set `apiKey` — it's sent as `X-Api-Key` on every request except /health.

request.description: Unauthenticated liveness check. `points: null` means the server is up but can't reach Qdrant (collection missing, or the service's own Qdrant connection is down).

The main endpoint: one question in, one grounded answer + sources out. This is what the chat widget calls per user message.

- `session_id` — one per chat widget instance/conversation thread. Reusing the same `session_id` across calls keeps conversation history (so "How long does it last?" resolves "it" from the previous turn). New conversation = new `session_id`.
- `declined: true` in the response means the question was out of scope (guard rejected it) — `answer` is a canned fallback message and `sources` will be empty; still a 200, not an error.
- 502 means the LLM call itself failed (HAWKI down/timeout) — safe to retry.
- 401 means a wrong/missing `X-Api-Key` (only if the server has one configured).

response.name: 200 OK (in-scope answer)
200 OK (declined — out of scope)
response.body:
{
  "answer": "Dazu finde ich leider keine passenden Informationen im Archiv.",
  "declined": true,
  "language": "de",
  "session_id": "drupal-test-session-1",
  "sources": []
}

request.description: Upload one or more PDFs (multipart, repeat the `files` key per file, max 50 per request). Chunks, embeds, and upserts into Qdrant, blocking until done — this is what the Node-RED flow calls on new/updated Islandora documents, not something the chat UI touches. Re-uploading a file with the same name overwrites its previous chunks (deterministic IDs).

Same as /ingest but returns immediately (202) with a job id per file; processing happens in the background. Poll GET /status/{job_id} for the outcome. Copy a `job_id` from the response into the `jobId` collection variable to use the next request.
Check the outcome of a job id returned by /ingest/async. 404 if the id is unknown (server restarted, or typo).
